subject: Model tranche, context needs and token estimate — onboarding sync
messages:
From: Sandra Kim <sandra@nextgenai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: liam.oconnor@nextgenai.com, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Onboarding next steps — context and traffic

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. To confirm a few items from our side before the engineering sync: our primary production use-case is document Q&A (user uploads + retrieval) with an expected avg doc length ~1,200 words and peak search sessions of ~12 RPS globally. We expect heavy tail for longer conversations (up to ~2.5k tokens in context) for multi-doc follow-ups.

Quick clarifying Qs:
- Do you expect the prefix/KV caching to cover our multi-query flows?
- If we start on a mid-sized model, what's the recommended immediate context window to avoid regressions while we iterate?

Also attached a small traffic sample and our procurement contact is on cc for contract timing.

—Sandra
Sandra Kim | Head of Product 
NextGenAI
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Kim <sandra@nextgenai.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model tranche, context needs and token estimate — onboarding sync

Hi Sandra — great summary and thanks for the sample. Short answers: yes on KV/prefix caching — it will help the follow-up queries if you can surface stable retrieval keys (e.g., doc id + vector id). For the first phase we recommend starting with an 8k context window to avoid quality cliffs on multi-doc chains, then narrow to 4k for cost optimization once you have steady prefix patterns.

I've attached a first-pass model tranche (3 tiers) and a provisional token estimate based on your traffic sample: see the spreadsheet. High-level numbers we used for the estimate below (monthly):
- Estimated active users: 12k
- Avg sessions/day per active user: 0.18
- Avg prompt tokens per session: 620
- Avg completion tokens per session: 410
- Monthly token estimate (prompt + completion): ~89M tokens

Notes: we modeled a 20% spike buffer for peak hours and included KV cache hit assumptions of 15% initially. If you expect higher cache reuse we can shave token spend further.

Next steps: we propose an implementation kickoff next Tue. Monica and Grace will run a short latency & cost simulation on our Dedicated config using the tranche models. Ben, can you confirm commercial milestones for the MAA?

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model tranche, context needs and token estimate — onboarding sync

Looping in commercial timing — procurement has signaled they want an MSA + MAA in parallel. We can do a 60-day pilot on a Reserved Dedicated pool with a consumption cap. I'll send an updated SOW and payment milestones to procurement (cc'd) by COB Monday.

Also: Nina from CS finance asked we include a run-rate projection for month-3 post ramp — I'll add that into the MAA draft.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nextgenai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, Sandra Kim <sandra@nextgenai.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model tranche, context needs and token estimate — onboarding sync

Thanks — quick technical note from our infra lead. When you say 8k window, do you mean per request final prompt assembled on our side (we use hashed doc segments) or on the server side after retrieval A/B merging? We want to ensure we don't double-send content in the prompt.

Also, our engineering preference would be: start with a 13B-class open quantized model if latency/throughput hits budgets — are there latency profiles in the tranche sheet for a 13B quantized variant?

On timeline: we can do kickoff Tue provided we have the MAA draft and a one-pager on the Dedicated instance specs (GPUs, concurrency, autoscale thresholds).

—Liam
Liam O'Connor | Platform Engineer, NextGenAI
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, Sandra Kim <sandra@nextgenai.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nextgenai.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model tranche, context needs and token estimate — onboarding sync

Quick internal wrap and ask before Tuesday kickoff:

1) Model tranche we recommend for pilot (attached):
   - Tier A (Quality-first): RedOpen-13B-q4 — 8k window — expected median latency 320ms @ 8 concurrent users per device
   - Tier B (Balanced): Llama-13B-quant — 8k window — median latency 260ms @ 12 concurrent users
   - Tier C (Cost-first): RedOpen-7B-quant — 4k window — median latency 140ms @ 16 concurrent users

2) Token buckets (month-1 projected with pilot traffic + 20% spike buffer):
   - Prompts: 56,000,000 tokens/month
   - Completions: 37,000,000 tokens/month
   - Total: 93,000,000 tokens/month

3) Ops asks for kickoff:
   - Redwood Dedicated SKU & instance spec doc (link included)
   - A small sample deployment recipe for KV prefix caching + retrieval dedupe (attached as a one-pager)
   - Confirmation from NextGen on whether the assembled prompt will be client-side or server-side (affects costs and token accounting)

Attachments included: model_tranche_shortlist_v1.xlsx, mutual_action_plan_NG-4721.pdf, traffic_sample_Jul-Sep.csv

If NextGen confirms prompt assembly is server-side, we'll provision a higher cache-estimate and re-run the token model (likely down ~8%). Otherwise numbers above stand as our conservative estimate.

See you all Tue — I will kick off the runbook and a quick latency sim on Dedicated tomorrow morning and post results in the Drive link.

—Monica
Monica Patel | Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
